job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let's talk about sports safety. Rohan, if you twist your ankle, what is the first thing you do? Rohan: I use RICE, but I keep walking on it to prove I am tough. Teacher: That is dangerous! RICE helps, but it is not a cure-all. If you feel severe pain, you must stop playing immediately. Even if you can still walk, the injury could be serious. Priya: I thought a sprain was an injury to a muscle. Teacher: Actually, a sprain affects ligaments, while a strain affects muscles. Also, never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling. Use ice instead. Rohan: What about concussions? If I don't faint, I am safe, right? Teacher: Not at all. A concussion is a brain injury that does not always cause fainting. Symptoms like dizziness or confusion might appear hours later, not just immediately. Priya: Should I stay in bed for days if I get hurt? Teacher: No, gentle movement is usually better than total bed rest once the initial pain settles. And remember, never wrap a bandage too tightly, as it cuts off circulation. Always listen to your body instead of trying to play through pain.

items.evidence: Even if you can still walk, the injury could be serious.
items.q: Meena twists her ankle during a match but can still limp around. What should she understand about her ankle?
options: Her ankle may still be badly hurt
Her ankle cannot be badly hurt if she walks
Her ankle will heal faster if she walks on it
Her ankle needs only RICE and nothing more
items.explain: The teacher says that even if you can still walk, the injury could be serious.

wrong.why: thinks being able to walk means the injury is not serious
thinks walking it off, like Rohan, is good for the injury
thinks RICE alone is enough, though the teacher says it is not a cure-all

items.evidence: Actually, a sprain affects ligaments, while a strain affects muscles.
items.q: Priya hurts a ligament in her wrist. Aman hurts a muscle in his leg. Which names their injuries correctly?
options: Priya has a sprain and Aman has a strain
Priya has a strain and Aman has a sprain
Both Priya and Aman have a strain
Both Priya and Aman have a sprain
items.explain: A sprain affects ligaments and a strain affects muscles, so Priya has a sprain and Aman has a strain.

wrong.why: thinks a sprain is a muscle injury, so swaps the two names
thinks a strain is a ligament injury at a joint
thinks 'sprain' is the name for any sports injury

items.evidence: Also, never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling.
items.q: Kabir puts a hot water bag on the knee he hurt a few minutes ago. What will most likely happen?
options: The knee will swell up even more
The knee will lose its swelling faster
The knee will heal fully within a few minutes
The knee will be fine if the bandage is tight
items.explain: Heat on a fresh injury increases swelling, so the teacher says to use ice instead.

wrong.why: thinks heat reduces swelling on a fresh injury
thinks the injury is healed once it feels better
thinks a tight bandage fixes everything

items.evidence: Symptoms like dizziness or confusion might appear hours later, not just immediately.
items.q: Arjun bumps his head at football but feels fine. That evening he feels dizzy. Which is the most likely explanation?
options: His dizziness comes from the head bump, just showing late
His dizziness comes from tiredness, since he never fainted
His dizziness comes from hunger, since head signs appear at once
His dizziness comes from the heat, since his pain had faded
items.explain: Concussion signs like dizziness can appear hours after the hit, and fainting is not needed for a concussion.

wrong.why: thinks there is no concussion unless the person faints
thinks concussion signs always show right after the hit
thinks the injury healed once the pain went away
